content.text: Energy doesn't just sit in stores—it moves. Understanding how energy transfers between stores is essential for analysing any physical process, from boiling water to powering a city. There are four main pathways by which energy can be transferred.
Energy transfers describe HOW energy moves between stores. The four pathways are mechanical work, electrical work, heating, and radiation.
(or energy pathway) is the mechanism by which energy moves from one store to another.

| Pathway | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| Mechanical (work) | Energy transferred by a force moving an object | Pushing a box, lifting a weight |
| Electrical | Energy transferred by moving charges (current) | Current in a circuit, lightning |
| Heating | Energy transferred due to temperature difference | Conduction, convection, radiation |
| Radiation | Energy transferred by waves (EM or sound) | Light from Sun, sound from speaker |

Dissipated energy is not 'lost' or destroyed. It has been transferred to thermal energy stores in the surroundings where it is spread out and difficult to use again.
— Energy is never lost, only transferred to less useful stores (usually thermal in surroundings).
— Heating is a transfer mechanism. The store is thermal energy.
— Electrical work is a transfer pathway, not a store. Energy is stored in chemical, kinetic, or other stores.
— Sound is a transfer mechanism (radiation). When we hear sound, energy is transferred to kinetic energy of eardrums.
— All solids conduct (metals are just better at it).

Chemical energy store (fuel) transfers energy by heating to thermal energy store (hot gases), then by mechanical work to kinetic energy store (pistons/crankshaft), then to kinetic energy store (wheels/car). Energy is also dissipated to thermal energy stores in the surroundings (exhaust heat, friction) and to sound.
— Wasted = 100 - 75 = 25 J. This energy is transferred to thermal energy stores (heat in the motor windings and surroundings) and some to sound. (calculation)

Radiation transfers energy from the Sun through space to the solar panel. The solar panel converts light energy via electrical work into electrical energy, which is transferred through cables by electrical work to appliances in the home.
